title: Modulated-energy relaxation, Faxen approximation and the pre-collision zero-thickness limit of finitely many slender rigid filaments
difficulty_reason: H2: the epsilon^2-inertia Newton equations are singularly perturbed and their ordinary total energy does not supply the required moving-configuration limit. The author compresses the forces using Lorentz reciprocity, defines modulated energy relative to the configuration-dependent Faxen velocity, and uses the independent shape-derivative estimate to control its time drift. The changing inertia and background-force terms are balanced against logarithmically small coercive resistance to obtain the epsilon^2 |log epsilon| relaxation scale with an explicit initial layer. A three-velocity comparison separates relaxation, static Faxen approximation at the actual configuration, and the limiting dynamics; its Gronwall position bound then closes the pre-collision separation/lifetime bootstrap. The complete drift-energy-bootstrap mechanism is an independent nonroutine H2 core. Compression identities, individual bootstrap lemmas and the main-theorem restatements are counted once within that core, with no newness-based grading, inherited static H3 or separately counted field-interpolation consequence.

editorial_notes: Exact author statement, full proof and complete work context retained; no assistant proof or corrected formula, added assumption or correctness certificate.

N is fixed and finite, the reference centerlines and cross-section maps are fixed, and distinct centerlines remain separated by a positive fixed d in local estimates. d_min is centerline distance; the source uses a separate C epsilon adjustment for solid-filament distance.

Use the original closed or Lipschitz non-closed filament model. Remark2.1's additional a_epsilon endpoint smoothing is only an unexpanded extension claim, not a newly completed smooth-endpoint theorem. No straight-rod, infinite-particle, post-collision or endpoint extension is added.

Proposition5.1 states a bound on nabla_(h,Q) of the bilinear strain-energy inner product. Its proof derives a delta-Lipschitz estimate between nearby configurations. Retain the actual gradient statement, both W1infinity times W2infinity terms, divergence-free W2infinity data and the fixed separation/small-epsilon quantifiers.

In the dynamical result the centerlines are non-straight and the normalized inertia matrices are positive definite and bounded uniformly in epsilon. Physical masses and inertias scale as epsilon^2 with fixed volumetric density; initial rigid velocities are epsilon-independent and initial mass-center offsets are of order epsilon.

The background pair has the original regover continuity into homogeneous H1 times L2 and bounded spacetime W2infinity times W1infinity regularity, with divergence-free velocity. No extra homogeneous Stokes equation for the background is assumed.

Proposition6.2 is an intermediate estimate on (0,T_epsilon,d); Proposition6.7 initially works on the stopped interval. Proposition6.4 closes the separation argument. Theorem6.5 and the kinematic part of3.4 are stated for every fixed T before the limiting first-collision time, for epsilon sufficiently small depending on T and separation.

Theorem6.5 approximates the exact velocity by the epsilon-dependent Faxen velocity evaluated at the actual thick-filament configuration, with error epsilon^2 |log epsilon| after the exponential initial layer. This is distinct from convergence to the decoupled limiting velocity, whose error includes |log epsilon|^(-1/2) exp(CT). Retain the initial mismatch term; no uniform velocity convergence down to t=0 without compatibility is asserted.

The exact source stopping-time display and other notation observations remain attached without correction.
